catalog_quote: 3. 1. Every word contains one or more vowels 5). Each vowel may be preceded by one consonant-phoneme or by none. Moreover a word always ends with avowel. If a vowel is followed by an identical vowel and they are not separated by a consonant, they sound like one vowd [sic] of nearly double the length. ... These "long vowels" behave in every respect in the same way as two (respectively three) different vowels and are accordingly written twice (or threefold). ... 3. 2. The word is marked by the word-accent. This word-accent consists of a high pitch of the penultimate vowel with a faint rising contour of the preceding vowels: ána, buéa, 1nawáa [scanned; = inawáa], akamekemekémo. I f the penultimate and antepenultimate vowels are identical and not separated by a consonant, they both have the high pitch: akokariáámo. Some loan-words have a different accent: sámala (religious contemplation), ljUni…

audit.deciding_source_year: 1952 (2nd ed. 1988, text of the grammar unchanged per the preface)
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation, the domain quotation and all three locators were found verbatim in the OAPEN scan we hold of Anceaux 1988 (PDF p. 18 = p. 9; p. 35; pp. 50-51). (2) Deciding source: a first-hand structuralist grammar (Glottolog: grammar sketch, 66 pp) by the language's principal describer, 1952, reissued unchanged 1988; it is the root source for Wikipedia, StressTyp and the Tryon CAD entry, and Glottolog/Crossref/archive.org show no later grammar, phonology or instrumental study of Wolio. (3) The only apparent conflict (StressTyp2 weight-sensitive U/P) is documented in the ST1 Remarks we hold as the compilers' own reanalysis of Anceaux's VV sequences as heavy monosyllables, not a different empirical claim; under either analysis accent falls on the penultimate vowel/mora, so our fixed-penultimate (vowel-counting, right-edge) coding stands. sources.note: StressTyp2's cited source for its weight-sensitive U/P coding of Wolio (our 'contra' entry); the ST passage we hold attributes plain penultimate stress with rightward shift under suffixation to it, so reading the 2-page phonology intro would let us close the contradiction note as a StressTyp reanalysis rather than a source disagreement, and adds the suffix-shift statement Anceaux 1952 leaves implicit.
